newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed down on Monday, but changed very little from the opening, in a quiet end to the month, traders said.
The weakness came as bunds softened and U.S. Treasuries lost their initial gains after an expected jump in U.S. August single-family home sales.
Traders said the Dutch market had hit a minor standstill. Sellers, they said, would only emerge as prices and spreads versus bunds increased.
"We see some sellers (of 10 year spreads) at 18 (basis points), so the spreads must go out further," one trader said.
On Monday, the 10 year bond/bund spread climbed to just short of 16 basis points.
Meanwhile, buyers were more interested in the higher yields available on bunds and French government bonds.

Few in the market were surprised by the Dutch decision, announced this morning, not to issue bonds in the final quarter of the year. Traders said they did not expect new issues until well into 1997 as upcoming redemptions were small and the Dutch government was likely to manage with short-term monetary instruments.
